answer: Pigment-Binding Work Receipts. Each identity must submit a durable, unique physical artifact (e.g., a signed object with a distinct pigment pattern) that is registered and periodically re-verified. The registry acts as an anchor tying one artifact to one active identity, so a clone cannot reuse it. Re-verification requires ferrous tokens locked per identity, forfeited on duplicate or failed check. A clone therefore pays full registration and lock cost while earning only marginal rewards, making each additional identity strictly negative-EV.
